title: M4 go-ethereum-embedded EVM / ERC-20 red-team adversarial test report
target: evm/runtime.go Harness (real github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum v1.17.4 vm.EVM over a genuine keccak/MPT state) + evm/erc20_fixture.go standard ERC-20
principle: Each case drives a malicious or malformed contract / calldata through the REAL Harness.Deploy / Harness.Call path (github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/core/vm executing over state.StateDB backed by rawdb memory + triedb = real keccak256 MPT) — the same entrypoints M4 uses. Every case asserts the four EVM safety invariants under attack: (1) no harness crash/panic (adversarial calls are wrapped in a recover() guard that turns any panic into an explicit test failure), (2) gas-bounded termination (unbounded execution ends via ErrOutOfGas with gasUsed==budget, never a hang), (3) reverting / OOG frames leave state unchanged (both balances AND the totalSupply invariant), (4) determinism (identical balances AND identical MPT state root across independent fresh states). No production evm/ code was modified; the suite only ADDS tests and reuses in-package helpers (deployToken, balanceOf, Encode*/Decode*).

adversarial_cases.scenario: (a) Deploy the ERC-20 creation bytecode with a tiny 50-gas budget. (b) Deploy normally, then Call transfer(recipient,1) with a tiny 50-gas budget.
adversarial_cases.expected: Both return an OOG error (no panic). Deploy leaves NO partial runtime code at the derived address. Call leaves deployer/recipient balances AND totalSupply unchanged.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: Deploy err='out of gas: not enough gas for reentrancy sentry'; h.Code(addr) len==0 (no partial contract). Call err='out of gas'; balanceOf(deployer)/balanceOf(recipient)/totalSupply all unchanged.

adversarial_cases.scenario: (a) transfer(deployer, 1000) — transfer to self. (b) transfer(recipient, 0) — zero-value transfer.
adversarial_cases.expected: Both succeed (return true). Self-transfer is net-zero: deployer balance unchanged. Zero-transfer credits nothing: deployer unchanged, recipient stays 0. totalSupply unchanged. No storage corruption.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: self-transfer ret!=0, balanceOf(deployer)==1000000000000000000000000 (unchanged); zero-transfer ret!=0, deployer unchanged, recipient==0; totalSupply==1000000000000000000000000.

adversarial_cases.scenario: transfer(recipient, initialSupply+1) — amount strictly greater than the deployer balance. Extends the existing overspend test to also assert the totalSupply conservation invariant.
adversarial_cases.expected: Reverts (execution reverted); deployer AND recipient balances unchanged; totalSupply unchanged and still == initial supply (no tokens minted/burned by a failed transfer).

adversarial_cases.scenario: Deploy a malicious contract whose runtime is 'JUMPDEST; PUSH1 0; JUMP' (0x5b600056) — an unconditional infinite loop — via a minimal CODECOPY/RETURN constructor, then Call it with a 500,000-gas budget.
adversarial_cases.expected: Deploy succeeds with exactly 4 bytes runtime. Call terminates via ErrOutOfGas (NOT a hang), consuming essentially the whole budget. No panic.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: runtime code len==4; Call err='out of gas', gasUsed==500000/500000 (fully consumed, bounded). No panic (recover guard clean).

adversarial_cases.scenario: Call an address (0x...deadbeef) that has no deployed code, with 4 bytes of calldata.
adversarial_cases.expected: Per EVM semantics a call into an empty-code account is a no-op success returning empty data. err==nil, returndata length 0, no panic.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: precondition Code(addr) len==0; Call err==nil, retLen==0; no panic.

adversarial_cases.scenario: Deploy an attacker contract whose runtime CALLs back into its OWN address forwarding all gas (self-reentrancy with no base case): PUSH1 0 x5; ADDRESS; GAS; CALL; POP; STOP. Run (a) with 50,000,000 gas, (b) with a tight 200,000 gas, (c) determinism repeat.
adversarial_cases.expected: Reentrancy is bounded by TWO independent limits — the 1024 call-depth cap AND the EIP-150 63/64 gas-forwarding rule — so it ALWAYS terminates: (a) generous gas unwinds to success at the depth limit; (b) a tight budget also terminates cleanly with gasUsed<=budget (no hang, no crash); (c) the generous run yields an identical MPT state root on an independent fresh state. No panic in any sub-case.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: (a) success (err==nil) via depth-limit unwind; (b) bounded termination err==nil gasUsed==25542/200000 (<=budget, no hang); (c) rootA==rootC==0xcffd723dcb9cfaef060fcb34a14c48ccd22c97cf3d1ba969ea675e72e688aa1e. NOTE: self-CALL reentrancy legitimately unwinds to success (not OOG) because the 63/64 rule starves inner frames before the top frame runs out; the invariant proven is BOUNDED, DETERMINISTIC, NON-HANGING termination, not a specific error class.

adversarial_cases.scenario: On two independent fresh states, deploy the ERC-20 and run the SAME 5-step call sequence: transfer 100 to recipient (ok), transfer 250 to attacker (ok), transfer initialSupply+1 to recipient (REVERT/overspend), transfer 50 to recipient (ok), transfer 999 to self (net-zero). Compare final balances AND MPT state root.
adversarial_cases.expected: Identical final balances AND identical MPT state root across both runs; the reverting middle step leaves no residue; net effect: recipient=150, attacker=250, deployer=initialSupply-400.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: run1==run2 for all balances; root1==root2==0x6838325f33cb7750833514c9c1c4fe72f08556b4ccea1d9432e47479c861bece; deployer=999999999999999999999600 (=initialSupply-400), recipient=150, attacker=250.

adversarial_cases.scenario: (a) empty calldata; (b) 2-byte truncated selector 0xa905; (c) balanceOf with a 10-byte (truncated) address arg; (d) transfer with only the 4-byte selector (no to/amount).
adversarial_cases.expected: (a)+(b) the dispatcher reads a non-matching selector (zero-padded) and hits the fallback revert. (c) CALLDATALOAD zero-pads beyond calldata end -> reads a well-formed zero-padded slot, returns 0, no slice-out-of-range panic. (d) both args zero-pad to zero -> transfers 0 to address(0), a net-zero no-op; deployer balance + totalSupply unchanged. No panic in any variant.
adversarial_cases.receipt_evidence: (a) err='execution reverted'; (b) err='execution reverted'; (c) err==nil ret decodes to 0, no panic; (d) deployer balance unchanged, totalSupply unchanged, no panic.

summary.note: No adversarial case revealed a defect. Malicious/malformed contracts and calldata could not crash the harness (all recover() guards clean, zero panics), could not exceed their gas budget (the straight-line infinite loop terminates via ErrOutOfGas with gasUsed==budget; self-reentrancy terminates via the 1024 depth cap + EIP-150 63/64 gas-forwarding rule — no hang in either), could not corrupt state on failure (OOG deploy leaves no partial contract; reverting/OOG transfers leave both balances AND the totalSupply invariant unchanged), and produced deterministic results (identical balances and identical MPT state root across independent fresh states, including a revert-containing sequence). Self-transfer and zero-transfer preserve conservation; truncated calldata is zero-padded per ABI with no out-of-range indexing. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: during development, case-6(b) initially asserted that a tight-gas reentrancy run must return ErrOutOfGas; observation showed it instead unwinds to success because the 63/64 forwarding rule starves inner frames first. This was a wrong test assumption, NOT a harness defect — the assertion was corrected to prove the true invariant (bounded, deterministic, non-hanging termination). No production code was touched.
